title: Maximum Execution Time Exceeded
description: Resolve PHP script timeout errors during updates, imports, backups, or slow admin operations.

steps.title: Identify the Timing-Out Action
steps.instructions: Record which URL, cron hook, or CLI command hits the limit. Check error logs for the script filename and approximate runtime.

steps.title: Increase max_execution_time
steps.instructions: Set max_execution_time in php.ini, .user.ini, or via set_time_limit(0) in wp-config for admin only. Avoid unlimited timeouts on public-facing requests.

steps.title: Use WP-CLI for Long Operations
steps.instructions: Run plugin updates, search-replace, imports, and regenerations via WP-CLI instead of the browser. CLI often has higher or no web timeout limits.

steps.title: Enable Batch Processing in Plugins
steps.instructions: Many import and migration plugins support chunked processing. Reduce batch size so each HTTP request finishes within the server timeout window.

steps.title: Move Heavy Work to WP-Cron or Server Cron
steps.instructions: Schedule large tasks during low-traffic windows. Use real server cron with DISABLE_WP_CRON and wp cron event run for reliability.

steps.title: Optimize Slow Queries Behind the Timeout
steps.instructions: Timeouts often mask slow SQL. Add indexes, clean revisions/transients, and disable plugins that query thousands of rows per page load.

steps.title: Retest Previously Failing Tasks
steps.instructions: Confirm imports, updates, and backups complete successfully. Document the final timeout settings and preferred run method (CLI vs admin).
